parts:
Hi,

I'm running Stan for part of my code which using the MCMC algorithm. Instead of using component wise (CW) MCMC, I'm using the NUTS sampler but, i didn't expect that it runs slower than CW MCMC.

I don't know whether my Stan programming skill is correct. It has been about 4 days and i got stuck in this stage of my work.

Your kind assistance on this is very much appreciated.
Thank you very much.

Hamed

P.s. I didn't show the whole code, but this the main part of my code which I'm showing for two different techniques as following: (Target distribution: Standard Normal, dimension of the problem: 1000)

nf_ini = 30; nf_ite  = 10; n = 1000
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- CW MCMC ------------------------------------------------------
for i=1:nf_ini                   % For each Markov Chain
ua(:,1,i)=x1(:,i);              % Initial state for the Markov Chain
gf(1,i)=g(i);                     % Corresponding g-value
count=1;l=2;
for l=2:nf_ite                   % Till nf_ite number of samples are obtained from each Chain
check=0;
for iii=1:n                        % Modified Metropolis-Hastings algorithm begins
ux(iii,1)=ua(iii,l-1,i)-0.5+rand;  % Uniform proposal density function
m1=normpdf(ux(iii,1));
m2=normpdf(ua(iii,l-1,i));
alpha=min(1,m1/m2);       % Acceptance ratio
if alpha>rand
ux(iii,1)=ux(iii,1);
check=check+1;
else
ux(iii,1)=ua(iii,l-1,i);
end
end
if check>0                       % Performance function is evaluated only when an unique sample is obtained
gx=pfn(ux,a,n);                 % pfn is just a function
if gx<g1
gf(l,i)=gx;
ua(:,l,i)=ux;
count=count+1;
else
gf(l,i)=gf(l-1,i);
ua(:,l,i)=ua(:,l-1,i);

else

ua(:,l,i)=ua(:,l-1,i);

end

Thank you very much for your prompt reply.

We can not use the Monte Carlo simulation. because, its main drawback, however, is that it is not suitable for finding small failure probabilities (Pf < 10^-3),
because, the number of samples, and hence the number of system analyses required to achieve a given accuracy, is proportional to 1/Pf.
Essentially, finding small failure probabilities requires information from rare samples corresponding to failure, and on average it would requires many samples before a failure occurs.

I attach both Matlab and Stan files for both CW-MCMC and NUTS via this email.

Thank you very much in advance for your time and consideration.
Hamed

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] NUTS through Stan running slower than traditional component wise MCMC in Matlab
parts:
To answer the original question, when you have a purely conjugate i.i.d.
model like yours, Gibbs reverts to pure Monte Carlo (MC) sampling, which is more
efficient than using NUTS to do Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC). You can code up
pure Monte Carlo in Stan, too, using the generated quantities block. Then it should
be just as efficient up to the normal RNGs being used.

More below.

> On Mar 14, 2017, at 1:07 PM, Hamed Nikbakht <hamednik...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> ...
> We can not use the Monte Carlo simulation. because, its main drawback, however, is that it is not suitable for finding small failure probabilities (Pf < 10^-3),

Right. Then you can't use MCMC either, which is even slower
to find small failures. It usually takes multiple MCMC
iterations to get the same power as a single MC iteration.
> because, the number of samples, and hence the number of system analyses required to achieve a given accuracy, is proportional to 1/Pf.

It's more that you only get about one useful draw for the tail
per 1 / Pf effective sample size.

You're going to have to either use some kind of truncation or
inverse CDF or something to code up tail probabilities.

- Bob

Thank you very much for the useful points that you mentioned.

I didn't get your point when you are pointing out "you can't use MCMC either, which is even slower
to find small failures.  It usually takes multiple MCMC iterations to get the same power as a single MC iteration."

In order to overcome the inefficiency of the Monte Carlo method in estimating small failure probabilities,
while maintaining its independency on the number of random variables, a method named Subset Simulation suggested by Au & Beck (which I'm using this technique) has been implemented.

This method express Pf as a product of conditional probabilities that are significantly larger than Pf. These conditional probabilities are estimated by application of MCMC sampling.
It should be noted that Subset Simulation has been studied in the mathematical literature under the surrogate terms Sequential Monte Carlo and Generalized Splitting.

THE POINT IS THAT the efficiency and accuracy of Subset Simulation depends of the ability of the applied MCMC algorithm to estimate accurately the conditional probabilities with minimum number of samples.

That's why I'm gonna recruit the NUTS sampling to see whether it can be improved with respect to the efficient sampling.

(The variance of the estimates of the conditional probabilities depend on the correlation of the Markov chains simulated by MCMC algorithm)

And My Matlab code is based on this subset simulation technique. I attach the figure for clarifying conceptually the subset simulation technique).

Your kind help on this is very much appreciated.

Hamed

parts:
We answered that one already. It's because "componentwise"
reduces to elementwise Monte Carlo in this case.

If you want to do pure Monte Carlo sampling in Stan, it
looks like this:

data {
int<lower=0> N;
}
model { }
generated quantities {
vector[N] x;
for (n in 1:N) x[n] = normal_rng(0, 1);
}

If that runs at different speed, it comes down to Boost's Normal RNG
vs. whatever package you're using. Make sure you're getting the right
results before comparing speed.

>>> > In order to overcome the inefficiency of the Monte Carlo method in estimating small failure probabilities,

>>> >
>>> > This method express Pf as a product of conditional probabilities that are significantly larger than Pf. These conditional probabilities are estimated by application of MCMC sampling.
>>> > It should be noted that Subset Simulation has been studied in the mathematical literature under the surrogate terms Sequential Monte Carlo and Generalized Splitting.

>>> > (The variance of the estimates of the conditional probabilities depend on the correlation of the Markov chains simulated by MCMC algorithm)

>>> > iterations to get the same power as a single MC iteration.
>>> >

>>> > It's more that you only get about one useful draw for the tail

>>> >
>>> > You're going to have to either use some kind of truncation or

>>> >
>>> > - Bob
